entities.summary:
Davide Ghirlandaio (1452–1525), also known as David Ghirlandaio and as Davide Bigordi, was an Italian painter and mosaicist, active in his native Florence.


Ghirlandaio was a prominent figure in the early Renaissance, known for his intricate frescoes and mosaics in the Chapel of the Maggior Ordine dei Cavalieri di San Stefano in Florence. His work was heavily influenced by the classical styles of ancient Greece and Rome, which were rediscovered during the Renaissance. Ghirlandaio's most famous work is the Chapel of the Maggior Ordine dei Cavalieri di San Stefano, which features over 250 figures in vivid detail.


Ghirlandaio's legacy extends beyond his own work, as he played a significant role in reviving the art of mosaics in Florence. His techniques and methods were adopted by other artists, including Michelangelo and Raphael, who went on to create some of the most iconic works of the High Renaissance.


Despite his influence on the art world, Ghirlandaio's life remains somewhat of a mystery. Little is known about his early life, and his personal relationships are shrouded in secrecy. However, his contributions to the world of art and architecture are undeniable, and his work continues to inspire artists and historians to this day.
